newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bond rise slows after rouble news.
newsitem.headline: Russian bond rise slows after rouble news.

text.p: A rise in long-term Russian OFZ interest-bearing bonds, which set in after recent falls, slowed after the government said it would issue a new rouble worth 1,000 old ones from next year, dealers said on Monday.
They said other government paper prices were virtually unchanged as banks did not transfer much money for the trading.
*Turnover fell to 2.66 trln rbls from 3.27 trln rbls on Friday
*Central bank did not intervene on the market on behalf of the Finance Ministry
*Yields of long-term T-bills were 18.58 pct after 18.51 pct
President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday that the government would chop three zeroes from rouble notes from January 1, 1998. Old and new banknotes will be in circulation for the whole of 1998.
"The day started well today. There were signs of OFZ growth, but after the announcement of the rouble redenomination it stopped," said Vneshtorgbank dealer Sergei Fyodorov.
"The fall is generally caused by market oversupply after extra trading sessions, but today it is caused by inertia."
The Finance Ministry has several times held extra trading sessions on Wednesdays, when trading does not usually take place, to soak up excess money after it repays tax-exempt government paper early.
The ministry will offer series 24011, 24012, 24013, 24014, 24015 and 24016 at an extra trading session this Wednesday.
Renaissance Capital dealer Alexei Orekhov said the trading plans would move prices further down on Tuesday as investors sold the paper to get a higher yield.
"There are no big flows from non-residents coming in and so the yields will remain stable," Orekhov said.
Dealers also said a big sell in series 24011 held the bond back.
